sections.html:
Family: Aspredinidae. Size: 3.5 cm. Temperature: 20–25°C. pH: 6.0–7.2. Synonyms: Dysichthys quadriradiatus, Bunocephalus quadriradiatus.

The species is listed as Data Deficient by the IUCN due to the paucity of records and because its exact range, population status and threats are not well known (IUCN 2016).
South America: Upper Amazon River basin of Peru. Type locality: Peru: Samiria, Chinguito [= Cocha Shinguita or Shirguita].
A very small species that can probably be kept as per other members of this family, in a quiet tank with sand and plants.

Pseudobunocephalus is distinguished from all other aspredinid genera by the following unique features: mandibular teeth restricted to a patch near the symphysis of the lower jaw; no contact between the metapterygoid and quadrate; autopalatine posteriorly forked with two separate cartilages; absence of the fourth pharyngobranchial; absence of gill rakers on all branchial arches; and lack of bifid hemal spines on vertebrae that articulate with anal-fin pterygiophores. As defined, Pseudobunocephalus contains a new species, P. lundbergi from the Orinoco River basin, along with five other species previously assigned to Bunocephalus: P. amazonicus, P. bifidus, P. iheringii, P. quadriradiatus and P. rugosus.

Etymology: The generic name combines the Greek word pseudes, meaning false or deceptive, with the aspredinid genus Bunocephalus. It alludes to the fact that members of this genus were previously mistaken for juveniles of various Bunocephalus species. The specific name quadriradiatus: quadri-, four; radiatus, rayed, referring to the four-rayed pectoral fin rather than the usual five.
